CHIEF COMPLAINT
Evaluation of abnormal renal ultrasound with atrophic right kidney.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Ashley is a 14-year-old female who presented with acute onset right-sided abdominal pain and was bent over in pain. Initial evaluation suggested appendicitis. She was treated for stomach virus with fluids at her primary care physician but worsened the next day. Subsequent ultrasound revealed one kidney was larger than the other. She was referred for further evaluation and imaging in Jacksonville, which revealed an atrophic right kidney that was significantly smaller than the left kidney. Additional findings included cysts on her kidney and ovaries, swollen lymph nodes, and an infection. She was treated in Atlanta for approximately four days with some improvement. She has not had vomiting since treatment but continues to complain of abdominal pain and burning sensation, especially when eating. She reports dysuria, particularly when drinking soda, but denies hematuria. Sometimes has difficulty initiating urination. Her parents suspect a severe infection affected her kidney at some point. Notably, at age 4, she was hospitalized three to four times for several days at a time with fever and symptoms treated with fluids and antibiotics, then the episodes resolved spontaneously.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Abdominal pain and burning sensation, especially when eating. Dysuria, particularly with certain beverages like soda. Difficulty initiating urination at times. Denies hematuria. No recent vomiting.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Previously healthy until recent presentation. Recurrent infections at age 4 requiring hospitalization multiple times over a couple of months, then resolved. Evaluated by gastroenterology and genetics; no clinically significant mutations found on genetic panel.

MEDICATIONS
Pepcid 40 mg daily. Claritin for allergies.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Significant family history of renal disease. Paternal grandfather had posterior urethral valves and obstructive neuropathy, developed chronic kidney disease, was dialysis-dependent, had a renal transplant which subsequently failed, and died at age 47. Paternal grandmother had breast cancer. Paternal great aunt has end-stage renal disease, chronic kidney disease stage 5, diabetes, and hypertension (diagnosed as an adult). Father, paternal aunt, and paternal cousins all have kidney issues.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Active in softball and interested in joining drill team over the summer. Lives with parents.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Well-appearing female, alert and oriented, sitting comfortably, not in acute distress. Lungs and heart sound great. Exam otherwise within normal limits.

RESULTS
Renal ultrasound shows atrophic right kidney, smaller than left kidney, with left kidney appearing larger possibly due to compensatory hypertrophy. Kidney function tests normal. Blood pressure normal. Urinalysis not yet performed at this visit. Previous imaging also revealed cysts on kidney and ovaries, and swollen lymph nodes.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
14-year-old female with atrophic right kidney, likely secondary to previous infection. Kidney function currently normal with normal blood pressure. At higher risk for developing hypertension and proteinuria. Plan includes annual monitoring with renal ultrasound to monitor kidney size and function, urinalysis to assess for protein and blood, and blood pressure checks. Avoid NSAIDs such as ibuprofen; use acetaminophen instead. Maintain adequate hydration with at least 2 liters of water daily, especially during sports activities. Encourage healthy diet and continue active lifestyle. Continue current medications. Follow-up with primary care physician or adult nephrologist closer to home; does not need to return to this facility for follow-up.
